q: 1. The number of independent equations to be satisfied for static equilibrium of a plane structure is
explain: For a planar (2D) structure, equilibrium requires three independent equations: ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, and ΣM=0.

q: 2. If the beam is supported so that there are only three unknown reactive elements at the support. These can be determined by using the following fundamental equation of statics
explain: Three unknown reactions require all three independent static equilibrium equations: sum of horizontal forces, sum of vertical forces, and sum of moments all equal zero.

q: 3. The moments in the arch will be zero, if
options: the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust
the arch axis is parallel to the line of thrust
explain: Bending moment in an arch is the product of the thrust and the eccentricity. If the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust, the eccentricity is zero, and thus the moment is zero.

q: 4. A three-hinged arch is said to be
explain: A three-hinged arch has exactly enough equations (including the extra condition at the third hinge) to solve all reactions using statics alone, making it statically determinate.

q: 5. The value of horizontal thrust produced in a arch is
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch carrying a UDL (w) over the entire span (L) with rise (h), the horizontal thrust H = wL²/8h.

q: 6. A roller support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the supports only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement but permits rotation
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base but does not permit any rotation
explain: A roller support allows movement parallel to the supporting surface (the plane of the base).

q: 7. A hinged support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the support only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement at all but permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
does not permit movement as well as rotation in any direction
explain: A hinged (pin) support restricts all translational movement but allows the members to rotate freely about the axes.

q: 8. The analysis of a structure is
options: deciding the material of the member
deciding the dimensions of the member
calculating the magnitude and nature of various straining actions at salient points of the structure
explain: Structural analysis is the process of determining the effects of loads (internal forces like shear and moment) on physical structures.

q: 9. A plane structure is structure
options: the various members of which lie in a plane
the thickness of various members of which will be very small
in which there will not be any bending moment
explain: A plane structure is defined as a two-dimensional structure where all members and applied forces lie within the same single plane.

q: 10. A plane structure which subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: If a structure designed only for in-plane forces is subjected to out-of-plane forces, it lacks the necessary constraints to resist that movement, making it unstable in that direction.

q: 11. A frame is completely analysed, when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: Complete analysis of a frame requires determining all internal actions, including axial (direct) stress, shear force, and bending moments across all members.

q: 12. The displacements of joints of a truss can be obtained directly from
explain: The Williot-Mohr diagram is a graphical method used to find the resultant displacement of all joints in a truss due to member deformations.

q: 13. The basic form of a pin jointed frame is
explain: The triangle is the simplest and only inherently stable geometric shape for a pin-jointed frame; other shapes require bracing to prevent collapse.

q: 14. A pin jointed plane frame with J number of joints and n, number of members will be internally redundant, if
explain: A truss is internally redundant (over-stiff) if the number of members (n) is greater than the minimum required for stability, which is given by the formula $$n = 2j - 3$$.

q: 15. A structure having J = 4 & number of member is 3 then structure should be
explain: For a plane truss, the condition for stability/determinacy is m = 2j - 3. Here, 2(4) - 3 = 5 members are required. Since there are only 3 members, the structure is deficient and unstable.

q: 16. Find the number of member in a structure if the number of joint is 4 for a determinate structure.
explain: Using the formula m = 2j - 3 for a determinate plane truss, where j = 4: m = 2(4) - 3 = 5.

q: 17. If the co moment of Joint A, B, & C are 10, 20 and 30 kN-m then find the balancing moment at joint B.
explain: In the Moment Distribution Method, the balancing moment is equal in magnitude but opposite in sign to the out-of-balance moment at the joint to maintain equilibrium.

q: 18. At a joint where several members meet, any applied moment will be distributed among the various members
options: equally among such members whose far ends are fixed
equally among such members whose far ends are hinged
explain: According to the principle of moment distribution, an applied moment is shared by members meeting at a joint in direct proportion to their relative stiffness (K).

q: 19. A horizontal beam with both the ends hinged will be statically determinate for this type of loadings
explain: A beam hinged at both ends has redundant horizontal reactions unless loading is purely vertical, in which case horizontal reactions are automatically zero, making it determinate only for vertical loads.

q: 20. Influence lines are drawn for structures
explain: Influence lines are a universal tool in structural engineering. While they are simpler to draw for determinate structures (linear), they are also used for indeterminate structures (where they are typically curved).

q: 21. Horizontal reaction at B as shown in fig. is equal to
explain: Summing horizontal forces (ΣHx = 0): The applied 10kN horizontal load at the top must be countered by an equal and opposite horizontal reaction at the support B to maintain equilibrium.

q: 22. In a general co planar force system, the number of unknown forces that can be found by the principle of statics is
explain: A general coplanar force system has 3 independent equilibrium equations: ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, ΣM=0, so up to 3 unknowns can be solved.

q: 23. Given pin jointed frame is (refer to image 1666)
explain: A frame is unstable if it doesn't meet the minimum member requirement ($m < 2j-3$) or if the arrangement of hinges allows for a mechanism.

q: 24. The function of king post in a roof truss is
options: to support the framework of the roof
to receive the ends of principal rafters
to prevent the walls from spreading outward
to prevent the tie beam from sagging at its centre
explain: The king post is a central vertical member that supports the tie beam below it, preventing it from sagging due to its own weight.

q: 25. The effective length of a column with both ends hinged is
explain: For a column hinged (pinned) at both ends, the effective length equals the actual length: Le = L.

q: 26. The maximum bending moment due to an isolated load in a three hinged parabolic arch (span l, rise h) having one of its hinges at the crown, occurs on either side of the crown at a distance
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch with crown hinge, standard analysis shows the maximum bending moment due to an isolated load occurs at a distance l/(2√3) from the crown.

q: 27. A cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load W over its full length is propped at its free end such that it is at the level of the fixed end. The bending moment will be zero at its free end also at
explain: For a propped cantilever with UDL and prop bringing the free end to the fixed-end level, analysis shows the bending moment is zero at the free end and again at 3/4 of the length measured from the free end.

q: 28. The bending moment in a cable carrying a system of loads will be
explain: A flexible cable, by its nature, can carry only axial tension and adjusts its shape (funicular shape) so that bending moment is zero everywhere along its length.

q: 29. In a pin jointed plane frame all the loads are assumed to act .............
options: in the plane of the frame
perpendicular to the plane of the frame
in a plane inclined at 45° to the plane of frame
explain: For a plane (2D) pin-jointed frame, loads are, by definition of the idealization, assumed to act within the plane of the frame.

q: 30. What is the maximum number of unknown reaction components that can be determined using only statics
explain: For a planar structure, only 3 independent static equilibrium equations exist, so a maximum of 3 unknown reaction components can be determined using statics alone.

q: 31. Castigliano's second theorem can be used to compute deflections
options: at the point under the load only
explain: Castigliano's second theorem, based on strain energy, is generally applicable to compute deflections in any type of elastic structure (determinate or indeterminate).

q: 32. The arches meant for supporting uniformly distributed loads, to avoid any bending moment must be
explain: For an arch to carry a uniformly distributed load (per unit horizontal length) with zero bending moment throughout, its shape must be parabolic, matching the funicular shape for such loading.

q: 33. The vertical distance of the crown of the arch above the springing is called
explain: The vertical height from the springing (support) level to the crown (highest point) of an arch is termed its rise.

q: 34. An arch can be treated as curved beam .............
options: whose ends are restrained against horizontal movement
whose ends do not provide any reaction
explain: An arch functions structurally as a curved beam whose supports restrain horizontal movement, allowing the horizontal thrust to develop and enabling the arch action.

q: 35. The moment in the arch will be zero if .............
options: the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust
the arch axis is parallel to the line of thrust
explain: Bending moment at any arch section equals the horizontal thrust times the perpendicular offset between the arch axis and the line of thrust; this moment vanishes only when the arch axis exactly coincides with the thrust line.

q: 36. The eddy theorem is valid for
explain: Eddy's theorem, which relates the bending moment in an arch to the vertical intercept between the arch and the linear arch (thrust line), is derived specifically for vertical loads.

q: 37. In a three hinged arch, the line of thrust .............
options: must pass through all the three hinges
must pass through two end hinges and may or may not pass through the third hinge
must not pass through any of the hinges
must pass through two end hinges only
explain: Since each of the three hinges in a three-hinged arch permits zero bending moment (M=0), the line of thrust must necessarily pass through all three hinge locations.

q: 38. The fixed support in a real beam becomes in the conjugate beam a
explain: In the conjugate beam method, a fixed support (zero slope, zero deflection) in the real beam transforms into a free end in the conjugate beam.

q: 39. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of joints; the number of equations of static equilibrium available is
explain: At each pin joint of a plane truss, only 2 equilibrium equations are available (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0), since moment equilibrium is automatically satisfied at a pin.

q: 40. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of sections, the section should be so chosen that it cuts
options: only three members at a time
any number of members but only two members with unknown forces
any number of members but only three members with unknown forces
explain: The method of sections uses 3 equilibrium equations (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣM), so a cutting section should pass through at most 3 members with unknown forces to be solvable.

q: 41. By assuming that all the forces acting on a pin connected truss are co planar and act at a joint only it can be expected that all the member will be subjected to
options: direct stress and shear stress only
explain: With loads applied only at joints (pins) and members assumed weightless/straight, truss members carry only direct (axial) stress — either tension or compression, with no bending or shear.

q: 42. In a pin jointed frame, it is sufficient if the forces in all the members meeting at a joint are .............
explain: For equilibrium at a pin joint (which cannot resist moment), it suffices that all member forces meeting there are coplanar and concurrent (passing through the same point).

q: 43. Internal forces at every cross section in a arch are
options: normal thrust, shear force and bending moment
explain: In general, an arch cross-section resists three internal force components: normal (axial) thrust, shear force, and bending moment, unless the arch axis coincides exactly with the thrust line.

q: 44. In a three hinged arch, the linear and the actual arch meet at
explain: Since the three hinges each enforce zero bending moment (meaning the arch axis coincides with the thrust line there), the actual arch and the linear (thrust-line) arch must intersect at least at these three hinge points.

q: 45. If a three hinged parabolic arch carries a udl over the entire span, then any section of the arch is subjected to
options: normal thrust, shear force and bending moment
explain: A parabolic arch under a matching uniformly distributed load has its axis coincide exactly with the funicular (thrust) line everywhere, so every section carries pure normal thrust with zero shear and moment.

q: 46. The number of reaction components possible at a hinge on rollers supports is
explain: A hinge-on-rollers support can resist only one reaction component: a force perpendicular to the rolling surface (vertical, typically), with no moment or horizontal reaction.

q: 47. m1 and m2 are the members of two individual simple trusses of a compound truss. The compound truss will be rigid and determinate if
explain: Since three additional connecting bars are needed to join two simple trusses into a stable compound truss, the total member count becomes m = m1 + m2 + 3.

q: 48. For a stable frame structure, number of members required, is
options: three times the number of joints minus three
twice the number of joints minus three
twice the number of joints minus two
twice the number of joints minus one
explain: For a stable, statically determinate pin-jointed plane frame (truss), the required member count is m = 2j − 3.
